title: Problems with Fractions of a Unit

steps.body: Measurements often land between whole units. A line plot in quarter-inches records eight marks at 1/4, and four of them rebuild one inch.
steps.narration: Measurements often land between whole units. A line plot in quarter-inches records eight marks at 1/4, and four of them rebuild one inch.

widget.prompt: On a whole-unit line, place where 8 quarter-unit lengths reach.

commonPlacements.feedback: One half uses two quarter-unit lengths; the plot contains eight.
Four wholes would require sixteen quarter-unit lengths, not eight.

widget.successFeedback: 2 whole units — eight quarter-units form two groups of four quarters.
widget.lowFeedback: This point is below the total of eight quarter-unit lengths.
widget.highFeedback: This point is above the total of eight quarter-unit lengths.

predict.reveal: Four quarter-inches make one inch, so eight of them group into exactly two.

cml.actionGoal: Recompose quarter-unit measurements into whole units.
invariants: Four quarter-units make one whole unit, so the total length is the quarter-unit count divided by four.
misconceptions: Reading the count of quarter-units as the same count of whole units.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A line plot records a total of 20 quarter-unit marks. What length do they represent in units?

commonErrors.feedback: 20 counts the quarter-marks; four of them rebuild one whole unit.
That multiplied by four. Quarter-units are SMALLER than units, so the number of units is fewer.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Group the quarter-units in fours because four quarters make one whole unit.

widget.prompt: Place a second total: where do 12 quarter-unit lengths reach on a whole-unit line?

commonPlacements.feedback: Three quarters uses only three quarter-unit lengths; the plot contains twelve.
Four wholes would require sixteen quarter-unit lengths, not twelve.

widget.successFeedback: 3 whole units — twelve quarter-units form three groups of four quarters.
widget.lowFeedback: This point is below the total of twelve quarter-unit lengths.
widget.highFeedback: This point is above the total of twelve quarter-unit lengths.

widget.prompt: Apply without the opening model: A line plot records lengths in quarter-inches. Eight marks sit at 1/4 inch. What total length is that?

options.label: 2 inches, because four quarter-inches make one inch
options.feedback: Correct — eight quarter-inches group into two whole inches, since each inch holds four of them.

options.label: 8 inches, because there are 8 marks
options.feedback: The marks count QUARTER-inches, not inches; eight of them is far less than eight inches.

options.label: 32 inches, because 8 × 4 = 32
options.feedback: Multiplying by four goes the wrong way — quarter-inches are smaller, so the inch count is fewer.

options.label: 1/2 inch, because 8 is bigger than 4
options.feedback: Eight quarter-inches is two whole inches; comparing the bare numbers ignores the unit.
